_readme: Curated from raw/capacity/CAPACITY_NOTE.md and raw/capacity/CAPACITY_DETAIL.md (2026-09-26 research pass). Every record carries {value, unit, source_title, source_url, page, tag, note}. tag one of VERIFIED (read the source document ourselves) / RELAYED (from a third party's summary/news, not the source document itself) / OPEN (no answer, or conflicting answers not yet resolved). Conflicting figures for the same quantity are kept as SEPARATE records sharing the same `key` so the conflict is visible side by side, never silently picked.

records.note: As-built design capacity of the existing drainage system, converted from the daily figure: 80 mm/day averaged over ~3 h/day of rain = 58.7 mm/h. Exact quote kept in docs/CAPACITY.md.

records.note: News reporting on the BMA-JICA drainage master plan describes 76 mm/h as the 'current' design criterion for NEW construction -- conflicts with the 58.7 mm/h VERIFIED as-built figure above. records.source_title: สถิติข้อมูลปี 2550, กองสารสนเทศระบายน้ำ สำนักการระบายน้ำ กทม.
records.note: Top-10 flood-prone roads by incident count in 2007: (1) สุขุมวิท 18x, (2) พหลโยธิน 16x, (3) ลาดพร้าว 15x (วังทองหลาง/บางกะปิ -- same zone as Sammakorn/Ram53), (4) งามวงศ์วาน 14x, (5) พระราม 6 14x, (6) พัฒนาการ 14x, (7) แจ้งวัฒนะ 13x, (8) ศรีนครินทร์ 11x, (9) ศรีอยุธยา 10x, (10) ราชสีมา 10x. วังทองหลาง has been a weak point for at least 18 years, not a new problem.
